title: Dans l'ascenseur avec Hippolyte  (In the Elevator with Hippolyte)

segments.t: Inside the ASK elevator, Mathias shares an uncomfortable private conversation with his son Hippolyte. They discuss Catherine's depression and Hippolyte's new relationship, before Camille greets Mathias in the lobby. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Comment va ta mère?
Le bromazépam est devenu son meilleur ami.
C'est toujours très gênant.
En tout cas tu es là.
J'ai besoin de prendre un peu de recul.
Je passe beaucoup de temps chez ma copine.
Tu as une copine?
Oui, c'est tout récent.
Bon, je vais y aller.
On s'appelle? Bien sûr.
Au revoir... Bonne chance pour ce soir!
Pardon, excusez-moi, Mathias.
Je vous passe votre prochain appel.
Let's examine how Mathias and Hippolyte share a quiet family moment step by step.
Comment va ta mère?
'How is your mother?' Mathias gently checks on Catherine using a standard greeting that literally asks how she goes. A standard way to speak in French.
Le bromazépam est devenu son meilleur ami.
'Bromazepam has become her best friend.' Hippolyte describes her reliance on tranquilizers using a direct cognate meaning 'best'. In French, you will hear this.
C'est toujours très gênant.
'It is always very awkward.' In the elevator, Hippolyte admits the situation is awkward using a handy connector meaning 'always'. The French say this often.
En tout cas tu es là.
'In any case you are here.' Mathias replies quietly using an everyday expression meaning 'in any case'. In French, this is quite common.
J'ai besoin de prendre un peu de recul.
'I need to get some distance.' Hippolyte explains his feelings with a handy chunk meaning 'to take a bit of distance'. This is how you say it in French.
Je passe beaucoup de temps chez ma copine.
'I spend a lot of time at my girlfriend\'s place.' Hippolyte explains his absence using a handy connector meaning 'at the home of'. A handy phrase in French.
Tu as une copine?
'You have a girlfriend?' Mathias is surprised by this unexpected news, addressing his son with the casual 'you'. A useful expression in French.
Oui, c'est tout récent.
'Yes, it is very recent.' Hippolyte confirms the relationship is new using a cognate meaning 'recent'. This is very typical in French.
Bon, je vais y aller.
'Well, I will get going.' Hippolyte prepares to exit the elevator using a filler meaning 'well', followed by a handy chunk for leaving. A common chunk in French.
On s'appelle? Bien sûr.
'We will call each other? Of course.' Father and son promise to stay in touch using a mutual action meaning 'we call each other'. You will hear this in French.
Au revoir... Bonne chance pour ce soir!
'Goodbye... Good luck for tonight!' As the elevator doors close, Hippolyte wishes his father luck which is a colorful slang expression. This is perfectly natural in French.
Pardon, excusez-moi, Mathias.
'Pardon, excuse me, Mathias.' Camille politely interrupts her father in the corridor using the formal 'you' to excuse herself. In French, it works nicely.
Je vous passe votre prochain appel.
'I am putting through your next call.' Back at his desk, Camille says she is passing the next call to him. The French use this a lot. Now let's listen to the conversation in the elevator once more.

Hippolyte leaves to meet his girlfriend, wishing his father good luck for the evening. Back in Gabriel's office, Sofia is furious after an explosive argument with casting director Constance. See you next time!
Au revoir... Merde pour ce soir!
